subject: Urgent: Elevated 5xx/429s from prefix cache thrash impacting BrightTrail - immediate action
messages:
From: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@brighttrail.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, support@redwood.com
Cc: Caroline Yang <caroline.yang@brighttrail.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: High 5xx/429s and timeouts since 09:50 - BrightTrail production

Hi Lauren / Redwood support team,

We've been seeing a large spike in 5xx and 429 responses starting around 09:50 PDT this morning. Our user-facing API calls to your hosted endpoints are returning intermittent 504s and many requests are seeing 429s followed by retries. Latency has spiked from p50 ~120ms to p50 ~2.7s and p95 >>10s. This is causing payment flows to fail in prod (we've had 6% failed checkout rate in the last hour).

Attached are a small excerpt of our logs and a latency chart. Please confirm receipt and give an ETA for mitigation. We need this prioritized — our CRO is asking for updates.

Attachments: support-logs-20260803.zip, latency-chart-10-18UTC.png

Thanks,
Alex
Sr. Platform Engineer
BrightTrail Health
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@brighttrail.com>
Cc: support@redwood.com, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429s and timeouts since 09:50 - BrightTrail production

Alex —

Thanks for the heads up and the logs. We have engineers looking at this now. Initial read shows a large increase in queueing on our inference layer and eviction spikes on the prefix cache for your tenancy.

Immediate plan:
- I have engaged the incident team (CC'd Dylan).
- We'll attempt a temporary routing change to bypass prefix cache and disable batching for BrightTrail traffic to reduce queue pressure.
- I'll update every 30 minutes with progress; if we can confirm a short mitigation window we'll propose a staged rollback of the cache policy.

We understand the impact and will prioritize.

—Lauren
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: URGENT: High 5xx/429s - likely prefix-cache + batching contention

Folks — forwarding customer thread. Summary: BrightTrail seeing 5xx/429 spikes, symptoms consistent with cache churn + batching-induced head-of-line blocking. Logs attached show repeated cache misses at the same prefix ranges and many small requests being batched which then overflow the serving queue.

Quick asks:
- Neha: can you drop batching for this customer (canary) and temporarily raise the cache TTL for prefix entries?
- Marissa: be ready to brief account execs on the mitigation and next steps (we may request an SLA credit).

I've attached the partial logs we received to the PagerDuty ticket.

Attachment: support-logs-20260803.zip (excerpt)

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Cc: eng-oncall@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: High 5xx/429s - likely prefix-cache + batching contention

Team — quick status update from infra: we've reproduced the pattern in staging with a synthetic traffic mix. Root cause appears to be a combination of:
1) aggressive continuous batching in the serving pool that groups many short requests into a single work item which then blocks the queue when a large request hits,
2) prefix cache eviction policy that thrashes under hot-key churn (small TTL + limited entry budget for the tenant),
3) a regression in a cache-metrics correction landed last week that caused TTLs to be shortened under burst conditions.

Mitigations applied at 10:40 PDT:
- Batching disabled for BrightTrail route (canary) — we saw p95 drop from ~12s to ~1.8s in the canary.
- Increased prefix cache TTL by 10x for their tenant; eviction rate dropped sharply.
- Enabled throttling backpressure to slow client retries (we returned a Retry-After header on 429s).

Customer metrics after changes (11:00 PDT):
- 5xx rate: from 3.4% -> 0.2%
- 429 rate: from 5.8% -> 0.6%
- p95 latency: from >10s -> ~1.9s

Next steps:
- Roll back the recent cache-metrics change and run a hardened test.
- Prepare a PR with a fix to the TTL logic and add an integ test for churn scenarios.

I'll coordinate with Marissa on customer comms. If leadership wants to pause rollouts until we ship the fix let me know.

—Neha
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: Urgent: post-incident summary and exec note for BrightTrail

Hi all —

Thanks for the rapid response. Customer note prepared below for execs/CS leadership; please review and suggest edits. Plan is to send this to BrightTrail's CTO and their CRO within the hour.

Draft customer-facing summary (short):
BrightTrail — we experienced elevated 5xx/429 rates between ~09:50-11:00 PDT due to a regression in prefix cache TTL handling combined with batching behavior that caused queueing and request timeouts. We implemented a canary mitigation at 10:40 PDT (disabled batching for your route, increased cache TTL) which reduced error rates and latency substantially.

Action items we are committing to:
- Immediate mitigation applied and monitored (done).
- Root cause fix: revert the TTL regression and ship a tested patch within 72 hours.
- Post-incident review and runbook updates to prevent recurrence; we'll share the RCA and the timeline for the fix.
- Offer: We'll propose a one-time service credit for the incident window; Marissa will coordinate.

If no edits I will send as-is and loop in our VP of Sales for the credit conversation.

—Marissa
Account Executive, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
